papers.title: 3D Bioprinting of Self‐Standing Silk‐Based Bioink
papers.abstract: Silk/polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels are studied as self-standing bioinks for 3D printing for tissue engineering. The two components of the bioink, silk fibroin protein (silk) and PEG, are both Food and Drug Administration approved materials in drug and medical device products. Mixing PEG with silk induces silk β-sheet structure formation and thus gelation and water insolubility due to physical crosslinking. A variety of constructs with high resolution, high shape fidelity, and homogeneous gel matrices are printed. When human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells are premixed with the silk solution prior to printing and the constructs are cultured in this medium, the cell-loaded constructs maintain their shape over at least 12 weeks. Interestingly, the cells grow faster in the higher silk concentration (10%, w/v) gel than in lower ones (7.5 and 5%, w/v), likely due to the difference in material stiffness and the amount of residual PEG remaining in the gel related to material hydrophobicity. Subcutaneous implantation of 7.5% (w/v) bioink gels with and without printed fibroblast cells in mice reveals that the cells survive and proliferate in the gel matrix for at least 6 week postimplantation. The results suggest that these silk/PEG bioink gels may provide suitable scaffold environments for cell printing and function.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文专注于丝素/PEG生物墨水的材料学与生物学验证，完全没有涉及AI或机器学习在生物打印中的应用。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML integration at any bioprinting stage; purely material and biological characterization without data-driven modeling or autonomous decision.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种自支撑的丝素/PEG生物墨水用于3D打印组织工程支架。
summary_zh.method: 混合丝素与PEG诱导β-折叠形成物理交联水凝胶。
summary_zh.result: 打印结构保持形状超过12周，细胞在高浓度丝素中增殖更快。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞培养和体内小鼠皮下植入验证生物相容性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a self-standing bioink based on silk fibroin and PEG for 3D bioprinting of tissue engineering scaffolds.
summary_en.method: Mixing silk with PEG induces β-sheet formation, leading to physical crosslinking and gelation without chemical crosslinkers.
summary_en.result: Printed constructs maintained shape fidelity for over 12 weeks, and cells proliferated faster in higher silk concentration gels.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and in vivo subcutaneous implantation in mice confirmed biocompatibility and cell survival for at least 6 weeks.
